article.content: Tampa Bay force Game 5 with extra-innings rally Milwaukee denied first World Series championship Brewers still hold 3-1 lead in best-of-seven series Jonny DeLuca and pinch-hitter Ben Williamson singled home runs in a stunning 12th-inning rally, and the Tampa Bay Rays staved off World Series elimination with a 4-3 win over the Milwaukee Brewers on Tuesday night that forced Game 5. Cooper Pratt hit a tiebreaking home run off Ian Seymour in the top of the 12th for his fourth hit of the game as Milwaukee neared a sweep and their first World Series title. Continue reading...
article.aiArticle:
The Tampa Bay Rays kept their championship hopes alive late into the night, manufacturing a dramatic 12th-inning rally to avoid a postseason sweep against the Milwaukee Brewers. According to Sport | The Guardian, the dramatic extra-innings surge forced a Game 5 in the best-of-seven series, denying Milwaukee a chance to secure their first-ever World Series title on the spot.

## Late-Inning Heroics Extend the Series

The decisive breakthrough came after hours of tense, scoreless or tightly contested playoff baseball, when Tampa Bay's offense finally broke through against the Brewers' pitching staff. The report states that **Jonny DeLuca** and pinch-hitter **Ben Williamson** delivered crucial base hits in the 12th frame, driving home the runs that completely turned the tide of the matchup. Despite the sudden loss, the Brewers maintain a comfortable advantage in the matchup as they prepare to take the field for the next contest. Prior to this stumble, Milwaukee had displayed dominant momentum, as detailed in our previous coverage of how [Ruthless Brewers close in on World Series sweep after crushing Rays 10-1 in Game 3](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/ruthless-brewers-close-in-on-world-series-sweep-after-crushing-rays-in). 

## Stakes and Immediate Aftermath

Context: World Series elimination games carry immense psychological and physical weight, draining bullpens and testing the depth of both organizations. For Tampa Bay, extending the series means avoiding the ignominy of a sweep while applying sudden pressure back onto their opponents. For Milwaukee, the missed opportunity delays what the franchise and its supporters have chased for decades—their maiden championship title. 

What to watch: Observers will be monitoring bullpen availability and starting pitcher stamina as both dugouts regroup for Game 5. The psychological shift from a potential celebration to a must-win scenario for Milwaukee will dictate how aggressively managers deploy their pitching rotations in the upcoming fixture.

Sources: [Sport | The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/oct/28/rays-brewers-world-series-game-four-12th-inning-rally)
